Update from Control – the 16:00 handback has officially been recorded. The track is certified and all systems are back to normal. Signalling is operating as expected and the crossing controls are in automatic mode. The severe thunderstorm warning is still active until 18:30, so please stay safe if you're still out and about.

### P. Hargreaves
15:12
Thanks Lou. All good here. I'm just finishing up the paperwork at the depot.

### J. Okafor
15:13
👍

---

**15:20**

### S. Delaney
I've just added the weather note to the handover sheet – rail temp at 41 degrees on the approach side, but within limits. Also added the storm warning times. The sheet is in the usual drive location if anyone needs to check it.

### T. Brennan
15:22
Thanks Sam. I'll review it tonight and get the roster sorted for Thursday week.

---

**15:30**

### M. Tran
Quick question about the Thursday week window – what time are we looking at? I've got a dentist appointment in the afternoon and I want to make sure I can make it.

### T. Brennan
15:31
Not sure yet. I'll know more once I've finalised the roster. I'll send it around tomorrow morning. If there's a conflict, let me know and we can sort it out.

documents.title: MRM Operations Channel
documents.content:
**15:40**

### S. Delaney
Just a heads up – the forecast has shifted for tomorrow arvo. The BOM update at 15:30 has the storms clearing earlier than first thought, but there's a chance of showers hanging around until late evening. I'll keep an eye on it and update the handover sheet if anything changes.

### T. Brennan
15:41
Thanks Sam. Noted.

---

**15:45**

### J. Kowalski
Has anyone seen the new track inspection checklist that was supposed to come through from the office? I thought it was meant to be circulated this week.

### R. Whitfield
15:46
I haven't seen it yet either. Might be worth chasing up with the office tomorrow.

### M. Tran
15:47
I saw a draft version last week, but not the final one. It had a few changes to the ballast profile section from memory.

### P. Hargreaves
15:48
I'll send a quick email to the office now to see where it's at.

---

**15:55**

### L. Delaney (Control)
Update – the severe thunderstorm warning has been downgraded to a minor storm warning, now due to expire at 17:30. Still some lightning about, so keep the usual precautions in place if you're working outside.

### S. Delaney
15:56
Cheers Lou. Good to know.

---

**16:05**

### T. Brennan
Roster update for Thursday week – I've had a look at the numbers and we're looking at a 06:00 start, with a planned handback around 14:00. The window is booked for 8 hours. I'll send the full roster around tomorrow morning as promised.

### M. Tran
16:06
06:00 start works for me. Dentist is at 15:30 so I'll be fine.

### J. Kowalski
16:07
👍

### R. Whitfield
16:07
👍

---

**16:15**

### P. Hargreaves
I've just heard back from the office about the checklist – it's still being finalised. The engineer wants to include a section on fastening condition assessments. Should be out by early next week.

### J. Kowalski
16:16
Thanks Pete. Good to know it's coming.

---

**16:25**

### M. Tran
Quick one – the fuel card for the Hi-Rail is playing up again. It worked fine this morning but it got declined at the servo on the way back. Anyone else had issues?

### R. Whitfield
16:26
Mine was fine yesterday. Might be worth checking with the office if the card has been deactivated or something.

### S. Delaney
16:27
I'll log it with the office tomorrow. In the meantime, use the spare card in the depot safe if you need fuel. The combo is still the same one from last month.

### M. Tran
16:28
Cheers Sam.

---

**16:35**

### L. Delaney (Control)
For anyone still on site – the minor storm warning has now expired. All clear. The rail temp on the approach side has dropped to 36 degrees and is still falling. Everything is within limits.

### P. Hargreaves
16:36
👍

---

**16:45**

### S. Delaney
I'm heading off for the day. I've left the handover sheet in the usual drive location with the weather notes and the storm warning times from earlier. The track certification paperwork from the 16:00 handback is also filed. Pete, you're on the evening check – anything I should know before I go?

### P. Hargreaves
16:46
All good Sam. I'll do the usual rounds and check the crossing controls are still in automatic mode. I'll update the sheet if anything comes up.

### S. Delaney
16:47
Thanks Pete. See you all tomorrow.

### T. Brennan
16:48
👍

---

**16:55**

### J. Kowalski
Actually, one more thing – I noticed the switch at the north end of the siding was a bit stiff when I was doing the certification checks this arvo. It wasn't flagged as a fault, but it might be worth having a look at in the next window. Just putting it out there.

documents.title: MRM Operations Channel
documents.content:
**MRM Operations Channel**

---

**17:05**

### L. Delaney (Control)
Update for the evening crew – the Bureau has issued a fresh wind warning for the coastal section from 21:00. Gusts up to 90 km/h possible. Nothing that takes us over the operating limits, but if you're doing the high-level inspections tonight keep an eye on the anemometer readings. I'll post the numbers here if they change.

### P. Hargreaves
17:06
Copy that. I'll factor it into the rounds.

---

**17:20**

### M. Tran
Does anyone know if the replacement point motor for the branch line junction has arrived yet? The delivery was supposed to be yesterday but I haven't seen any paperwork.

### S. Delaney
17:22
I checked with stores this morning – they said it was on the truck from Melbourne. No ETA past that. I'd ring them tomorrow if nothing shows up.

### J. Kowalski
17:23
I'll chase it up in the morning. If it's not here by Wednesday we might need to push the replacement window back. I'd rather not, but we can't do the swap without the unit.

---

**17:35**

### R. Whitfield
Bit of a random one – the inspection camera on the drone is playing up. It's fine on the ground but the feed drops out when we get past about fifty metres altitude. We've tried two different batteries and it's the same every time.

### P. Hargreaves
17:36
Could be the transmitter. We had a similar issue with the old one and it turned out to be a loose antenna connection. Worth checking before you send it away.

### R. Whitfield
17:37
Ta, I'll have a look at that tomorrow.

---

**17:50**

### T. Brennan
Just finished the evening visual inspection of the bridge approach. All good, no obvious issues. The flood debris from last week has been cleared properly. I've put the photos in the shared drive under "bridge inspections – May".

### L. Delaney (Control)
17:52
Thanks Tom. Noted.

---

**18:05**

### P. Hargreaves
For anyone doing the night shift – the crossing lights at the Mill Road level crossing are showing a steady green for road traffic at the moment, which is correct. I've checked the fault log and there's nothing outstanding. The gate arms are moving freely after the earlier service.

---

**18:20**

### J. Kowalski
Question about the possession plan for Friday – are we still running with the single track closure from 23:30 to 04:30, or has that changed? I need to update the crew roster and I don't want to book people for the wrong shift.

### L. Delaney (Control)
18:22
As far as I know it's unchanged. The paperwork went through this afternoon. I'll double-check the final version in the system and confirm if there's any variation.

### J. Kowalski
18:23
Cheers. I'll wait for your confirmation before I send out the roster.

---

**18:40**

### M. Tran
The Hi-Rail is back in the depot and refuelled with the spare card. I've left the keys in the office. Also, the tire pressure on the rear passenger side was a bit low – I've topped it up but it might be worth getting it checked properly.

### S. Delaney
18:41
👍

---

**18:55**

### R. Whitfield
Quick heads up – I noticed some graffiti on the signal post at the south end of platform 2. It's not affecting anything operationally but I thought I'd flag it. I'll grab a photo tomorrow if it's still light enough.

### L. Delaney (Control)
18:56
Thanks. We'll log it with the graffiti removal crew. Not urgent unless it's obscuring a signal aspect – you said it's not, so we're fine.

---

documents.title: MRM Operations Channel
documents.content:
**19:10**

### R. Whitfield
Just had a look at the weather radar. There's a big band coming through overnight, looks like it'll hit us around 02:00. Rain's heavy, the kind that sets in. Might be worth reminding the night crew about the low-lying section near the creek – if it comes up like it did in March we could have some surface water on the track.

### L. Delaney (Control)
19:12
Thanks for the heads up. I'll put a note in the night handover. We've got the pumps on standby at the underpass, they were serviced last week so should be right.

---

**19:25**

### T. Brennan
Re the rain – I've checked the culvert at the north end of the yard and it's clear. The grate was half covered with leaves so I've cleared that too. Should be fine unless we get a real downpour.

### P. Hargreaves
19:27
Good work Tom. I remember that culvert blocked up in Feb and the yard was a mess for a day. Glad it's sorted.

---

**19:40**

### J. Kowalski
Anyone know if the night crew has the high-vis rain gear? I've got a couple of spare sets in the locker but I think a few of the newer blokes might not have their own yet.

### S. Delaney
19:41
I think there's a box of them in the stores. I'll check in the morning and let you know. If anyone needs one tonight, the spares in the locker are fine to use.

### J. Kowalski
19:42
Ta. I'll mention it at the pre-start.

---

**19:55**

### M. Tran
For the night shift – the track inspection trolley has a new battery, charged and ready. Also the floodlight is working again, the wiring was loose. It's in the back of the shed if anyone needs it.

### L. Delaney (Control)
19:56
👍

---

**20:10**

### R. Whitfield
Just a reminder – the wet weather procedure says we need a visual check of the cutting at the 42km mark if rainfall exceeds 25mm in 12 hours. I've had a look at the gauge and we're at about 12mm since this morning, so not there yet, but the overnight band could push it over.

### P. Hargreaves
20:12
Good point. I'll put it in the night handover so they know to check it if the rain gets heavy.

---

**20:25**

### T. Brennan
The graffiti on the signal post – I got a photo this evening, it wasn't too dark. I've put it in the shared drive under "signal post graffiti – May". It's just a tag, not obscuring anything.

### L. Delaney (Control)
20:27
Thanks Tom. I'll forward it to the removal crew tomorrow. Not urgent.

---

**20:40**

### J. Kowalski
Re the possession plan for Friday – L. Delaney, did you get a chance to confirm if it's still the single track closure from 23:30 to 04:30? I'm about to send out the roster and want to make sure I've got it right.

### L. Delaney (Control)
20:42
Just checked the system – it's confirmed as the single track closure, 23:30 to 04:30. No changes. I'll send you the final copy now.

### J. Kowalski
20:43
Beauty. Thanks for that. Roster goes out tonight.

---

**20:55**

### S. Delaney
Weather update – the bureau has issued a severe weather warning for the region, mostly for heavy rain and possible flash flooding in low-lying areas. It's in effect from 23:00 tonight through to tomorrow afternoon. Nothing about hail or damaging winds, but the rain is the main concern.

### R. Whitfield
20:57
Thanks for that. I'll make sure the night crew knows. The creek crossing at the 38km mark is the one to watch – last time it came up quick.

### L. Delaney (Control)
20:58
We've got a spotter assigned for that crossing if it gets bad. I'll confirm they're on for tonight.

documents.title: MRM Operations Channel
documents.content:
**21:10**

### S. Delaney
Just got the radar update – the band is moving slower than expected. The 25mm mark is still possible but likely closer to 2am than midnight. I've updated the night handover to say check the cutting at 42km around 3am if it's still raining then.

### R. Whitfield
21:12
Good. The cutting's been stable since the last washout, but better to look.

---

**21:25**

### P. Hargreaves
For anyone doing the morning check – the sump pump at the underpass near the depot is making a noise again. It was serviced last week but it's got that squeal back. I've logged it in the fault book. Not urgent but it'll need a look before the next big rain.

### L. Delaney (Control)
21:27
Thanks Pat. I'll add it to the list for the depot crew tomorrow.

---

**21:40**

### T. Brennan
The signal post graffiti photo is in the drive now. I also noticed the fence panel near the 40km mark is loose – the one that was hit by the tree branch last month. It's leaning a bit more than it was. I didn't touch it, just flagged it so it doesn't get forgotten.

### R. Whitfield
21:42
I'll take a look in the morning if the weather holds. If it's going to come down, better to secure it before it ends up on the track.

---

**21:55**

### J. Kowalski
Roster for Friday is out. Sent it to everyone's email. If there's any issue with the times, let me know before Thursday arvo. We've got the standard crew plus two extras for the possession – both are familiar with the single track closure setup.

### L. Delaney (Control)
21:57
Received. Looks good.

---

**22:10**

### S. Delaney
The severe weather warning has been extended – now in effect until 6pm tomorrow. Flash flooding is still the main risk. The bureau is saying up to 60mm possible in some areas, mostly west of us. We might get less but it's worth planning for.

### R. Whitfield
22:12
Thanks. I'll pass that to the night crew. The creek crossing at 38km is the one to keep an eye on – last time it came up quick.

### L. Delaney (Control)
22:14
Spotter is confirmed for tonight. They'll be at the crossing from midnight unless the rain eases off before then.

---

**22:30**

### P. Hargreaves
Quick question – the wet weather procedure mentions a visual check of the cutting at 42km if rainfall exceeds 25mm in 12 hours. But it also mentions the embankment at the 45km mark. Is that still a thing or was it removed from the procedure? I don't see it in the current version.

### R. Whitfield
22:32
It was removed in the last update – the embankment was stabilised two years ago and they took it off the list. The cutting at 42km is the one that still needs checking.

### P. Hargreaves
22:33
Right, thanks. I was looking at an old copy.

---

**22:45**

### T. Brennan
The floodlight in the shed is working again – the wiring was loose. It's in the back if anyone needs it.

### L. Delaney (Control)
22:47
👍

---

**23:00**

### S. Delaney
Rain has started here at the depot. Light so far but the radar shows the heavier band is about 30 minutes out. I'll post an update if it gets heavy.

### R. Whitfield
23:02
Copy that. I'll be on the radio if anything comes up.

---

**23:15**

### J. Kowalski
One more thing on the Friday possession – I've had a look at the plan and the single track closure is from 23:30 to 04:30. We've got the first inspection slot at 23:45 and then the crew can start on the rail grinding from midnight. The ballast work is scheduled for the second half of the possession.
